channel.title: Pointegrity Journal
channel.description: Decisions, reasoning, and work-in-progress notes from the team building Pouch at Pointegrity.

item.title: The part that got slower
item.description: AI assistants write code in seconds now, and the obvious conclusion is that everyone is faster. Writing was never the whole job — deciding whether the code is right used to come bundled with typing it, and now it does not. The slowdown is hard to feel from the inside, and better models make the surviving mistakes harder to see rather than fewer.

item.title: Borrowing the shape, not the box
item.description: NotebookLM made the grounded-notebook surface general — point at your sources, chat, get cited answers. This is about the harder half: generalizing the depth. Structure-aware parsing instead of blunt chunks, typed entities projected from a stable layer and re-projected as the schema changes, answers that cite their sources, and a model that stays in the building. We borrowed the shape; the box was the part worth keeping.

item.title: The bench we kept rebuilding
item.description: Several of our recent chat-and-canvas apps kept showing up with the same bones — different domain, same scaffold. liugent (liu as in 流, flow) is the scaffold factored out: a small Go bench plus a plugin slot where the domain lives. First plugin is internal, used live during TWSE hours. Notes from the workshop, not a product announcement.

item.title: The games we kept in a drawer
item.description: A short break from the serious mini-apps. We dug two small math games out of the drawer and rebuilt them clean — Domino Solver, a partition puzzle, and Cat and Mouse, the 19th-century pursuit game Conway analysed in Winning Ways. Both a small collaboration with the Chiu Chang Mathematics Education Foundation, and a reminder of what a break is for.

item.title: The attic, and the noise we found in it
item.description: A new piece of the family: attic, the backup layer behind pouch, mytraces, and the rest. A polite email from the cloud provider about high outbound traffic turned into a small forensic dig — a few hundred megabytes of actual data was producing several hundred gigabytes of cross-region traffic a week. The mismatch was in how we'd set up the safety net, not in any of the apps.

item.title: The state that hid behind the map
item.description: Notes from rebuilding the bottom sheet in mytraces, a trip-companion app shipping soon. A back-button gesture that opened a Discover modal turned out to be a follow-up tap landing on an invisible chip — and the chase exposed a deeper pattern in how state was scattered across modules. Three architectural slices later, a lesson about where view-coordinated state should live.

item.title: The bag, with pockets
item.description: A few days reshaping the pouch home view on the phone. Stream-bound drops collapse into pockets, pinned items sit at the top without a label, search moved to a corner icon. Plus a small affordance — a gear on each stream card — that pays the biggest dividend.

item.title: What the codebase remembers
item.description: A passing note about poi, the typed knowledge index our codebase has been quietly accumulating about itself. Gotchas with file-glob triggers, decisions you stop re-litigating, boundaries that are real gates. Internal dogfood for now — notes from the workshop, not a product announcement.

item.title: The ontology pattern, in three domains
item.description: The same architecture we use in mytraces (travel) shipped first as SC PreAlgebra (math), and now in a third domain — SC Programming. Why this shape keeps showing up in our work, and what it deliberately doesn't try to be.

item.title: The ontology and the model
item.description: A status report from inside mytraces, our internal trip-planning project. Why we're building it around two pillars — a curated ontology and an LLM — and how that decision is shaping the work. Internal dogfood for now, design notes worth writing down.

item.title: What we built while the journal was quiet
item.description: Ten days off the journal. A status report from the workshop floor: a visual-identity system shared across our app family, schema housekeeping in the auth library, real test coverage for previously-untested layers, and the honest answer to the marketing question. Plus a real subscribe form below.

item.title: Paid from day one: why pouch skipped the free tier
item.description: The indie-SaaS default is free-tier-then-upsell. Pouch chose the opposite. Here's the reasoning on alignment, signal quality, and infrastructure math — plus why the trial is 14 days specifically, and the one case where this framing might fail.

item.title: One type system for app and content: why we picked IBM Plex
item.description: System fonts were the safe default. Inter was the obvious indie-SaaS pick. We went with Plex — and this post is set in it. Why one coordinated family beats a stapled-together pair.

item.title: Streams, not folders — why pouch chose policy lanes over hierarchy
item.description: Folders are the obvious default. Here's why pouch said no, and what a "stream" does that a folder doesn't. The decision that keeps pouch from drifting into note-app shape.

item.title: Why pouch: what it is, what it deliberately isn't
item.description: Pouch kept getting pulled toward "note app" or "dropbox" framings. Both were wrong. Here's what we chose instead — a "personal data relay" — and the product decisions that cascaded from it.
